positions.name: ForgetZeppelinScopeDirective
positions.frame: when a directive commands erasure of a knowledge domain the graph never actually captured, what governs whether and how that domain is treated as in scope?
positions.why: Both segments are imperative erasure directives from the same actor on the same date, targeting adjacent slices of one named domain (the freight fleet plus its helium contracts, then the routes) — same performed act, same flat calm-negative register, same coercive/informational power read, same authority-ranking relational stance, same decision-grade conviction (universal quantifiers 'everything'/'all', no argument offered), same conservation-coded value framing of erasure as returning to a clean baseline. Pass-2 found no existing node in the perspective this domain could bind to, so the pair coheres as a single directional read: an authority-issued scope-exclusion command aimed at material this graph does not actually hold. Held in tension: the directive presupposes the material was once known, while the graph's own state shows it never was — that gap is narrated, not resolved.
